title: Microsoft Purview DLP: act on classification failures in Exchange Online (Worldwide)
notes: claim 50: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the detection switch, its PowerShell command and the administrator-enabled default, and the roadmap facts match. Narrow the statement about when senders notice the change; the checklist also names rule controls missing from the controls table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Exchange Online DLP policies can detect and act on classification failures where the service cannot fully scan a document.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policies for Exchange Online can detect and act on classification failures—cases where the classification service can't fully scan a document.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page is titled Configure default protection for classification failures in Data loss prevention for Exchange (preview) and describes the preview.
claims.quote: Configure default protection for classification failures in Data loss prevention for Exchange (preview)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Classification failure detection is admin-opt-in, with the new detection requiring administrator enablement.
claims.quote: By default, these conditions detect only text extraction failures. After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: With detection off, Document couldn't be scanned and Document didn't complete scanning detect only text extraction failures, not classification failures.
claims.quote: By default, these conditions detect only text extraction failures.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Text extraction failure examples include a file that cannot be opened, an unsupported format and a password-protected file.
claims.quote: Text extraction failures (for example, the file couldn't be opened, the format is unsupported, or the file is password protected).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: After enablement, the two scan conditions also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling and other errors.
claims.quote: After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures lets a rule take different actions for Timeout, Throttled or Other classification failures.
claims.quote: To take different actions for specific classification failure types—Timeout, Throttled, or Other—use the DocumentScanFailures condition.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures must be combined with Document couldn't be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning using AND.
claims.quote: Combine it with either Document couldn't be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning using AND

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures cannot be used on its own.
claims.quote: DocumentScanFailures can't be used on its own.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The detection setting applies to Exchange Online only.
claims.quote: This setting applies to Exchange Online only.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The setting does not affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams or Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: It doesn't affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, or Endpoint DLP policies.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Enable detection in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange > toggle.
claims.quote: from the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Settings on the left navigation menu > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange. In Scan failure settings for Exchange turn on the toggle.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json in Security & Compliance PowerShell sets classification failure detection.
claims.quote:
Connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell and run the following commands.
Connect-IPPSSession
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.where: controls[0].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: The enabling value of $json is the JSON string {"Classification":{"State":1}}.
claims.quote: $json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0

claims.where: controls[0].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting Classification.State to 0 with the same command disables detection.
claims.quote:
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.quote: Allow up to one hour for the setting change to synchronize across the service before validating policy behavior.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Detection is a single tenant-level Exchange Online setting.
claims.quote:
To enable classification failure detection, you can update the setting in the Purview portal or use PowerShell.
If your tenant already has rules that use these conditions, you might see an increase in DLP rule matches after you enable detection.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing rules using the two scan conditions might produce more DLP rule matches after detection is enabled.
claims.quote: If your tenant already has rules that use these conditions, you might see an increase in DLP rule matches after you enable detection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers DLP has already evaluated.
claims.quote: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers that DLP has already evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A classifier failure in a content-detection rule placed after a scan-failure rule will not be detected by that scan-failure rule.
claims.quote: If a content-detection rule is placed after a scan-failure rule and its classifier fails, the failure won't be detected.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft advises giving content-detection rules higher priority than scan-failure rules.
claims.quote: To avoid missed detections, order your rules so that content-detection rules (sensitive information types, exact data matches, and trainable classifiers) have higher priority than scan-failure rules (Timeout, Throttled, Other)

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Learn ordering example places content rules at priorities 1–3 and scan-failure rules at 4–6.
claims.quote:
Content rules at priorities 1–3.
Scan-failure rules at priorities 4–6.
The following table shows an example that follows this pattern.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The Learn example uses Block for its content-detection rules.
claims.quote:
| 1 | Detect credit cards | Content contains Credit Card Number | Block |
| 2 | Detect account numbers | Content contains Account Number | Block |
| 3 | Detect EDM match | Content contains EDM SIT | Block |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Learn example uses Audit for Timeout, Throttled and Other scan-failure rules.
claims.quote:
| 4 | Full scan timeout | DocumentIsUnsupported AND DocumentScanFailures = Timeout | Audit |
| 5 | Partial scan throttling | ProcessingLimitExceeded AND DocumentScanFailures = Throttled | Audit |
| 6 | Other scan errors | DocumentIsUnsupported AND DocumentScanFailures = Other | Audit |

claims.claim: The Exchange conditions reference lists DocumentScanFailures as a Security & Compliance PowerShell condition parameter.
claims.quote:
Condition/Exception parameters in Security & Compliance PowerShell
Document scan failures | Condition: DocumentScanFailures | N/A | Recommend using with Document could not be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning conditions

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The feature page describes no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-PolicyConfig DlpErrorHandlingConfig classification failure roles permissions message outcome detection disabled. Read the full feature page; it documents portal and PowerShell configuration, scan conditions and rule ordering, not a new identity model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The feature page names no per-user or per-policy scope for the detection switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-PolicyConfig DlpErrorHandlingConfig classification failure roles permissions message outcome detection disabled. Read the feature page and Set-PolicyConfig reference; the feature page names no per-user or per-policy detection switch.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Set-PolicyConfig reference does not list -DlpErrorHandlingConfig at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-PolicyConfig DlpErrorHandlingConfig classification failure roles permissions message outcome detection disabled; searched full fetched Set-PolicyConfig reference for DlpErrorHandlingConfig. Absent from syntax and parameters; present on feature page.

claims.where: Open questions: message outcome
claims.claim: The feature page does not describe the message outcome when a scan fails and detection is off.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-PolicyConfig DlpErrorHandlingConfig classification failure roles permissions message outcome detection disabled. Read full feature page; it states default detection capabilities but no message delivery outcome with detection off.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Actions on matching messages are defined by the DLP rules.
claims.quote: Conditions in Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies identify sensitive items that the policy is applied to. Actions define what happens as a consequence of a condition being met.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: Senders notice the change only if a rule they trigger blocks or flags a message whose attachment failed to scan.
claims.quote: Searched: Exchange DLP classification failure detection sender impact notifications audit only. Read feature page and Exchange conditions/actions reference; they document configurable actions but do not establish blocking or flagging as the only sender-visible outcomes.
claims.fix: Remove 'only': replace the sentence with 'Senders may notice the change if a rule they trigger blocks or flags a message whose attachment failed to scan.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; controls
claims.claim: Every rule control the governance checklist tells administrators to review or configure appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Plan rule priority so content-detection rules sit above scan-failure rules' and 'Add rules that combine DocumentScanFailures with one of the two scan conditions using AND.' Table: 'Whether Exchange Online DLP detects classification failures' only.
claims.fix: The checklist steps that review scan-condition rules, choose per-failure-type actions, set rule priority and add DocumentScanFailures rules have no corresponding controls row. Do not add rows as part of this correction.
